title: They weren’t just tall.
paragraphs:
They weren’t just tall.
They were a warning.
Before the flood… before Noah built the ark… before rain ever touched the earth…
“The Nephilim were on the earth in those days—and also afterward—when the sons of God came in to the daughters of man…” — Genesis 6:4 (ESV)
The Bible doesn’t waste words—and yet here, it opens a door to a mystery that still shakes theologians, historians, and believers today.
Where did the giants come from?

Some scholars interpret this as fallen angels crossing a boundary God never intended—producing a generation of corrupted strength. Others see it as the collision of the godly line of Seth with the rebellious line of Cain—creating powerful men who abandoned righteousness and became legends of violence.
The text doesn’t obsess over how they came.
“The Lord saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth… every intention of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.” — Genesis 6:5

A world where power had no conscience.
Where desire overruled obedience.
Where influence replaced integrity.
The Nephilim weren’t just physical beings.
Evidence of what happens when humanity drifts from God.

When boundaries blur.
When sin is normalized.
When people stop trembling at His Word.
That judgment came like a flood.
“And God saw the earth, and behold, it was corrupt, for all flesh had corrupted their way on the earth.” — Genesis 6:12
Your giant may not carry a spear.

• The addiction you keep justifying
• The secret you hope no one finds
• The anger you call “personality”
• The pride you disguise as strength
And it whispers the same lie:
“You come to me with a sword and with a spear… but I come to you in the name of the Lord of hosts…” — 1 Samuel 17:45
Because giants don’t fall by size.
They fall by surrender to God.
David didn’t defeat Goliath because he was skilled.
He won because he knew Who was with him.
And that’s where grace walks in.
Because the greatest giant wasn’t Goliath.
No stone could bring it down.
No human strength could outrun it.
“The Word became flesh and dwelt among us…” — John 1:14
Jesus didn’t come to study giants.
At the cross, the biggest enemies—sin, death, shame—were confronted head-on.
“He is not here, for He has risen, as He said.” — Matthew 28:6
That’s the turning point of history.
The moment every giant lost its final authority.
Because Jesus didn’t just fight for you.
“In all these things we are more than conquerors through Him who loved us.” — Romans 8:37
This isn’t just a story about ancient giants.
Wondering if this is the battle that breaks you.
“This is the battle where you finally trust Me.”
If something in your heart is stirring… that’s not guilt.
You are not alone in the valley.
The same God who flooded the earth to cleanse it…
The same God who empowered David to stand…
The same God who raised Jesus from the grave…
